(i) there is an increasing availability of a wide range of psychotropes, (ii) the use of psychotropic drugs for enhancement purposes (ie, to improve normal functioning) raises important philosophical issues, (iii) these issues are best addressed by a naturalistic conceptual approach that is based on the results of cognitive-affective science, and (iv) this conceptual framework can be used to address the enhancement debate in a way that is both theoretically and practically useful.
the use of psychotrophs for enhancement purposes is not justified.

how we should think about the use of psychotrophic agents in a wide variety of contexts.

the enhancement debate is best understood as a debate about the appropriate role of psychopharmacological agents in the context of a range of other factors (eg, social and environmental factors) that influence human flourishing.
